chat.author: Christian Huitema
chat.text: Do I understand correctly that this would be a replacement for dualQ-AQM, more suitable for routers "in the network" with DualQ is used "at the edges"?

chat.author: Chris Box
chat.text: That is my understanding, yes. It's a queuing implementation for high capacity routers that don't have the resources to implement a large number of DualQs.

chat.author: altanai
chat.text:
I was wondering about the same but my AI tells me that ---->
instead of coupling the queues via a shared delay controller (like DualPI2), SRM divides the work across three hardware stages

Packet Classification (Splitting Traffic)
Ingress Policing on the L4S Queue Only
Priority Scheduling (Draining the Queues)

chat.author: Zaheduzzaman Sarker
chat.text: my understanding is it provides alternatives for the high capacity routers

chat.author: Christian Huitema
chat.text: And that would work by having a strict priority, L4S > classic, combined with setting a peak bandwidth for L4S, so there is always bandwidth left for CE?
